groups.title: Burns: Rinse, Remove, Soak, Cover, Transport
items: Rinse: run cool water over the burn for 15 to 30 minutes.
Remove: carefully take off or cut away clothing around the burn while it's in the water. Leave any part stuck to the wound, and don't break blisters.
Soak: keep it in cool water for about 30 more minutes. For large burns, children, or older adults, don't soak too long, to avoid getting too cold.
Cover: cover it with clean gauze. Don't put ointment or home remedies on it.
Transport: get to a hospital as soon as possible.

blocks.source: Sources: Health Promotion Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare; Taipei City Fire Department; All-out Defense Mobilization Agency

groups.title: Heavy bleeding
items: Call 119 first, then control the bleeding while you wait.
Arms and legs: press on the wound with clean cloth and keep the pressure on. If it doesn't stop, tie a tourniquet 5 to 8 cm above the wound and note the time.
Head, neck, chest, abdomen: don't use a tourniquet. Press gently around the wound with clean cloth. Don't pull out anything stuck in the body.

groups.title: Someone collapses and doesn't respond
items: No response: ask someone to call 119, and check for normal breathing.
Not breathing normally: ask someone to bring an AED and start CPR. When the AED arrives, turn it on and follow the voice prompts.
Still breathing: turn them on their side to keep the airway open.
